decisionsTitle: The ship says whether production answered, and a stopped release can be re-labelled (amending §426, §535)
decisionsSection:
**Context (2026-10-03).** The release of `BR-V2.65` from the phone waited 59 minutes 35 seconds in ship's production wait while the club's domain was on a registrar hold. The log said «waiting for BR-V2.65-2026-10-03 on production», then «STOP: production never reported BR-V2.65-2026-10-03» — the same two lines it prints when production answers with another build. `health()` swallowed the fetch error and returned an empty body, so ship itself could not tell the cases apart. Then the run's closing comment and the removal of the `ship` label were refused («Resource not accessible by personal access token»): the label stayed on, and adding it again could start nothing. Both cost the owner an evening.

**Decision.**

- **One reading, judged.** `scripts/ship-checks.mjs` gains `judgeProductionReading({ body, error }, expected)`, pure and tested, returning one of four kinds: `no-answer` (a fetch error, described by its cause — «TypeError fetch failed — ENOTFOUND <host>: a name or network failure», a refused connection, a certificate, a timeout), `other-build` (the body names another baseline), `expected`, and `unreadable` (an empty body or an HTML page: a hold or parking page, a proxy's error). `health()` in `scripts/ship.mjs` returns `{ body, error, status }` instead of an empty string.
- **The waits say what they see.** Both production waits (step 1 for the previous baseline, step 7 for the new one) run through `waitForProduction`. It prints on the first reading and then every two minutes, not on every 20- or 30-second poll. The three readings in its words:
  - «no answer for 12 min: TypeError fetch failed — ENOTFOUND <host>: a name or network failure; docs/RUNBOOKS.md § The domain stops answering»;
  - «production answers with BR-V2.64-…; waiting for BR-V2.65-…»;
  - «production answers but its body carries no baseline (HTTP 200, no baseline in the body)».
- **The STOP names the case.** «production never reported <baseline> — <the last line>» and «production did not report <baseline> in time — <the last line>», with «check Vercel's production deployment» added when another build answers. The STOP's first line is the times file's `outcome`, so the summary page's table says it too. The PR comment also carries it: «The release stopped (failure) — ship: <outcome> — …». The final «production: …» line is unchanged.
- **The comment and the label use the job's own token.** `release.yml`'s `permissions` gain `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`. The step «Say so on the pull request» runs with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. A comment or a label changed by GitHub's token starts no workflow, which is right: only a person adding the label must start a release. Every push, merge and approval keeps `SHIP_TOKEN`, because what GitHub's token pushes or merges starts no workflow (§535). `contents` stays `read`. The label comes off through the REST call (`gh api -X DELETE …/issues/<PR>/labels/ship`), not `gh pr edit`, which also reads the pull request's projects, more than the job's token is granted. The token no longer needs **Issues** (`SETUP.md` § 41); a token that has it may keep it.

**Refused.**
- A shorter wait. The hour at the start and the twenty minutes at the end are right for a deploy that is slow; what was missing was the words, not a shorter clock.
- A retry of the label by the workflow itself. After a STOP, a person decides when production is ready and ticks the label again; the workflow never re-labels or restarts itself.

**Amends §426 and §535 (2026-10-03).** §426's ship gains a judged production reading next to its judged checks. §535's «Say so on the pull request» writes with the job's token, and the job's permissions are no longer read-only. `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` § Release from the phone and `docs/DISPATCHER.md` § Ship say what the log says now and what to do in each case.
changelogLine: - **The release says whether production answered** — while it waits for production, ship prints every two minutes whether the site did not answer (with the network error), answers with another build, or answers with a page that carries no baseline, and its STOP, the summary page and the pull request's comment name the case; the comment and the `ship` label's removal now use the run's own token, so a stopped release can be labelled again. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given `yarn ship`, when it waits for production to report a baseline, then it judges each reading as no answer (naming the fetch error's cause), another build (naming its baseline), the expected one, or a body with no baseline. It prints what it sees on the first reading and then every two minutes, and its STOP names the same case. Given `.github/workflows/release.yml`, the closing comment carries that STOP, and the comment and the label's removal run with the job's own token, which may write pull requests and issues; every push, merge and approval runs with `SHIP_TOKEN`. Verification: unit `scripts/ship-checks.test.ts`, `scripts/release-workflow.test.ts` (2026-10-03, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
